title: Book 5 — Terpsichore, Chapter 113
paragraphs: So Artybius, the commander of the Persians, fell there on the spot together with his horse. While the others too were still fighting, Stesenor, the tyrant of Curium, deserted them, having with him a large force of men—these Curians are said to be colonists from Argos—and when the Curians had deserted, forthwith also the war-chariots of the men of Salamis did the same as the Curians. When these things happened, the Persians had the advantage over the Cyprians; and after their army had been routed, many others fell, and among them Onesilus son of Chersis, the man who had brought about the revolt of the Cyprians, and also the king of the Solians, Aristocyprus son of Philocyprus—that Philocyprus whom Solon the Athenian, when he came to Cyprus, praised in verse above all other tyrants.
